To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the decrease of abundance of the diatom P. sulcata in surface water with increasing wind was more pronounced in the summer.

the decrease of diatom concentrations at higher winds was much influenced by the seasonal conditions: the reduction was more pronounced in the summer, when the surface concentration of diatoms decreased substantially with increasing winds.

1) the decrease of diatom concentrations at higher winds was much influenced by season; 2) in summer the surface concentration of diatoms decreased substantially with increasing winds, while in winter the decrease was less pronounced; 3) the reduction of cell numbers was possibly linked to changes in sinking of particles due to the altered cell density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the wind and temperature on the distribution of diatoms in the German Bights.
the seasonal variations of the diatoms' distribution in the water column in response to changes in the sinking and resuspension processes.
the analysis of the influence of wind on the abundance and distribution of diatoms in the German Bights.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reduction of sinking speeds of particles due to the increased temperature and salinity of the water column is the most important factor determining the decrease of diatom concentrations in the surface water.
the seasonal changes in sinking of planktons are the most likely cause of the observed changes in the distribution and abundances of diatoms in the German Bights.
sinking of plankton particles was reduced in summer due to the higher temperature and salinity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the seasonal variability of sinking of plankton-like particles is an important process influencing the distribution of species in the water column.
the reduction of sinking speeds of particles in the winter period is a possible explanation for the observed seasonal differences.
the seasonal changes of the diatom abundance in the German Bights are mainly caused by the seasonal variations in sinking of diatom cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the seasonal variability of the sinking of planktonic cells is an important mechanism controlling the distribution of diatom cells in the water column.
the seasonal variability of the sinking of plankton-like particles is a key mechanism influencing their distribution in the water column.
the sinking rate is a key parameter controlling the distribution of plankton-- like particles in the water column.
